title: A quick end-of-month budget check before October starts
dek: September ends tomorrow, and a ten-minute look at my accounts tonight helps me start October without surprises.
body: Tomorrow is the last day of September, which means a lot of bills, renewals and autopays are about to reset for a new month. Before I go to bed tonight, I like to spend about ten minutes looking at where the money went this month.

I keep it simple. I open my bank app and scroll through the month once. I am looking for three things: any charge I do not recognize, any subscription I forgot I had, and any category that got bigger than I expected. I do not judge myself while I do it. I just notice.

Most months, something small turns up. It might be a streaming service I signed up for to watch one show, or a free trial that quietly turned into a paid plan. Canceling one of those before the new billing cycle feels like finding a few dollars in a coat pocket.

I also check which bills come out in the first week of October. Rent and a couple of utilities land right at the start of the month for me, and knowing the dates ahead of time keeps me from spending money that is already spoken for.
Tonight, pick one subscription or recurring charge and ask yourself if you would sign up for it again today. If the answer is no, cancel it before October begins.
